Entry 1: the reviewer's two trees — a block documenting a neighbouring declaration, and code lines between the block and the declaration — are refused at this head, and so are my own variants of them (a block closed several declarations above, a trailing block comment on an intervening declaration, a comment run broken by a blank line), each with its twin that must still pass. Entry 2: the suite reports `Results: 83 passed, 0 failed` before my red test, and `jj diff --from 0c5d413f48e4 --to @-` on the test file is `144 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)` — additions only, so my round-2 case is byte-identical and still present. Entry 3: the literal and quote traps behave as it says — a URL inside a string, a quoted `/* … */` on a code line and a regular-expression literal holding both tokens are all code, so the declaration is refused; a `/*` inside a `//` comment and a `//` inside a block are credited to the comment they sit in; apostrophes and backticks in the comment break nothing. The numeric gate is unregressed, which I proved first rather than assuming: all twelve round-1 trees and all four octal trees keep their verdicts, and both AGENTS.md assertions still hold in both directions. The failure below is one the implementer's own negative control claims not to exist, so its proof is sound on what it measured and wrong on what it generalised.

The architect's four shapes, each with its twin: a comment run broken by a blank line (refused; unbroken, accepted); a block closed several declarations above (refused; adjacent, accepted); a trailing block comment on an intervening declaration (refused; the same block on its own line, accepted); a string or regular-expression literal holding `/*` or `*/` (refused both ways).

My four additions: a URL inside a string above the declaration is code (refused) while the same URL inside a `//` comment is credited; apostrophes and backticks inside the comment break nothing; a `/*` inside a `//` comment belongs to that comment (accepted when it names the other constant, refused when it does not) and a `//` inside a block belongs to the block; the declaration's own trailing comment passes naming `maxInputChars` and is refused naming nothing.

Round 3's shapes all retained and still right, including two the new direction improves: a block whose closing line starts with `//` is now credited (round 3's graded observation is fixed by the downward read), and an unterminated `/*` written as a real comment is credited while its stray `*/` counterpart is not.

observations: The one structural note I would want the next round to have: both the climb and the downward read answer `is this line comment text?` with a token test, and a token inside a string literal is indistinguishable from one that opens a comment without tracking quotes — which the implementer deliberately does not do, for a good reason (both real comments carry apostrophes, and a naive quote tracker would refuse the real tree). The two requirements meet in exactly one place, a line that opens with `/*` and never closes it, which is the failure above. A rule that treats an unterminated `/*` as opening nothing — crediting only blocks whose close is found — satisfies both without parsing strings, and fails closed where it is unsure.

Unchanged and still out of scope, as every round: an ask's embedded text is `question || ' ' || coalesce(answer->>'text','')` and a document's markdown is cut at the same limit with the same silence (dispatch://INFRA-114 owns both); the generated copies of the cap are held by `bun run check:go` in a job main's ruleset does not require.
